Ju-Kao Engineering Co Ltd Reports Solid Revenue Growth in Latest Financial Results

Taipei—Ju-Kao Engineering Co Ltd, a prominent player in Taiwan’s engineering and construction sector, reported robust financial results for its latest quarter, buoyed by steady infrastructure demand and a growing backlog of public works projects.

According to financial disclosures released Thursday, Ju-Kao Engineering posted a 9.8% year-on-year increase in revenue, reaching NT$2.05 billion for the quarter ended March 31. Net profit rose 7.3% to NT$194 million, driven by improved project execution and cost efficiencies across its portfolio of civil engineering contracts. Gross margin for the period climbed to 12.4%, compared to 11.6% a year earlier.

Chairman Chen Wei-han attributed the company’s performance to “disciplined project management and our ongoing focus on high-value segments, including transportation infrastructure and utilities.” He added, “We continue to see healthy demand from both government and private sector clients, particularly as Taiwan advances its long-term infrastructure development initiatives.”

Ju-Kao Engineering’s order backlog stood at NT$9.6 billion at the end of the quarter, up from NT$8.9 billion in the prior period. The company secured several significant contracts in the first three months of the year, including a municipal water treatment facility in Taichung and the early phases of a light rail extension in Kaohsiung. Management said these projects reflect the government’s ongoing investment in urban development and environmental upgrades.

Analysts welcomed the results, noting that Ju-Kao Engineering has demonstrated resilience despite a competitive bidding environment and rising input costs. “Their ability to maintain margins while expanding top-line revenue speaks to operational strength,” said Lin Chih-feng, an analyst at Formosa Securities. “We expect continued momentum, particularly if new infrastructure tenders accelerate in the second half of the year.”

The company’s balance sheet remains healthy, with a reported cash balance of NT$1.2 billion and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.31. Capital expenditures totaled NT$52 million for the quarter, largely allocated to the acquisition of new machinery and technology upgrades.

Looking ahead, Ju-Kao Engineering said it expects to benefit from sustained infrastructure spending in Taiwan, especially in transport and energy projects. The company reiterated its commitment to enhancing productivity and pursuing selective opportunities in renewable energy construction, an area highlighted for future growth.

Shares of Ju-Kao Engineering Co Ltd closed up 1.7% on the Taiwan Stock Exchange following the results announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the company’s outlook and execution.
